facebook.content_angle: Six-beat kick efficiency — how most competitive swimmers default to a two-beat kick and surrender 10% of their 50m speed without knowing it
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers are leaving a full second on the table — and their kick is why. 🦵

If you're grinding out 50m reps and your times have plateaued, the problem probably isn't your pull. It's what your legs are doing between strokes.

👉 A two-beat kick keeps you afloat. A six-beat kick drives your rotation, stabilises your hips, and generates propulsion on every single stroke cycle.
👉 Swimmers who switch to a disciplined six-beat kick pattern see up to 10.21% improvement in 50m times — not from fitness gains, but from mechanics.
👉 The kick isn't a float device. It's your engine.

This winter block is exactly when that engine gets built. ⚡

✔️ Start with a vertical kick set — 6x25m kick-only with fins, no board, arms at your sides
✔️ Drill tempo: two kicks per arm entry, every stroke, every lap
✔️ Film yourself from the side — if your hips are dropping, your kick timing is off

What does your kick look like mid-race — are you working it or just surviving?
